question:
This letter could have been written by anyone, and that is the problem. Only you know the details that would make it unforgettable.

Steps:
1. Use the arrow tool to point at a sentence that anyone could have written.
2. Use the text tool to rewrite it with at least one detail from the “Only I know” card (or from your own life).
3. Record your voice explaining what makes your version yours, and what you would keep from the AI’s version.

rubric.description: No arrow or text is placed on the board, or the voice recording is missing or blank.
Student places an arrow, but types no rewrite.

Arrow points to a sentence anyone could have written (sentence 1, 2, 3, or 4) AND the typed rewrite includes at least one specific detail from "Only I know" or the student's own life AND the voice recording names one thing that makes the new version theirs.

Meets all of the above AND the typed rewrite includes at least 2 specific details and a feeling or opinion AND the voice recording names one thing from the AI version worth keeping (such as the structure).

whiteboard_starter_image_alt_text: "A letter an AI wrote for a time capsule": "Dear Future Reader," followed by four numbered sentences: 1, "I hope this letter finds you well."; 2, "Right now, technology is changing fast and life is busy."; 3, "I hope the future is bright and full of good things."; and 4, "Take care of the world." It is signed "Sincerely, a student from the past." A card labeled "Only I know" lists: My cat, Waffles, knocks everything off the shelf. The bakery on 5th Street smells like cinnamon every morning. My little brother calls the moon "the night cookie." Below the card is a blank box labeled "Space for your rewrite."
